thread:
incident-bot: PAGING: Streaming API p99 latency spike detected for model-route /v1/stream (region: us-west) — auto-escalation to incident channel. SLO breach: p99 > 800ms. Runbook: <https://redwood.runbooks/streaming-latency>
jess-oncall: Got the page, I'm on it. Looking at grafana now. anyone see recent deploys or profile changes? @deploy-bot?
deploy-bot: Recent rollout: precision-profile:int8-calib-2026-03-14-22:18 applied to ~12% of traffic for model: rwd-llama-13B. No rollbacks.
alex-sre: Confirming spike started ~22:30 UTC, coincident with that rollout. p95 jumped from 120ms -> 320ms, p99 from 420ms -> 980ms. Streaming stalls (stall count spikes) observed in the same window. attaching quick query results.
priya-eng: that's the int8 calibration patch I pushed (small canary). I rolled a tweak to KV cache alignment and a new dequant kernel selection. didn't expect stalls.
elaine-cs: CS: we have 3 customers opened tickets about increased latency and partial stream truncation. Severity: medium (some UX timeouts). Keeping them informed.
morgan-runtime: grabbing runtime logs. early glance shows repeated "kv_cache_miss" and "dequant_wait_io" traces from the int8 hosts. also seeing backpressure to router queues. copy of grep:
```
2026-03-14T22:31:02Z host-int8-04 runtime: kv_cache_miss key=conv-xyz
2026-03-14T22:31:02Z host-int8-04 runtime: dequant_wait_io us=4132
2026-03-14T22:31:03Z host-int8-04 router: stream-chunk-delay queue=15 len=240
```
sam-oncall: Routing tiers show 12% of requests hitting int8 canary pool, but those requests have 4x tail variance.
jess-oncall: Okay. Immediate mitigations: (1) abort int8-calib rollout, (2) switch canary traffic to fp16 fallback variant, (3) scale up fp16 pool by +2 nodes. Priya, can you revert the precision-profile toggle?
priya-eng: on it. Reverting via config-store: `cfg set precision-profile rwd-llama-13B canary disabled --txn=quick` -> running.
priya-eng: Revert command applied. Confirmed: precision-profile int8-calib rolled back from 12% -> 0% within 30s.
deploy-bot: Config change recorded in deploy-log id=cfg-7923, triggered by priya-eng.
morgan-runtime: Traffic now shifting. fp16 fallback receiving the diverted traffic. initial metrics: p99 down to ~480ms and trending. stream stalls decreasing but still above baseline.
jess-oncall: Good. Next: Are there any hotpatches required for KV cache logic? alex, any ideas on why dequant_wait_io spiked?
alex-sre: My guess: the int8 kernel selection for long-context streaming introduced synchronous dequant calls that contend with disk-backed KV prefills when cache miss rate grows. We seeing correlated disk I/O waits on those hosts.
priya-eng: I can push a serialized-prefill patch but prefer to triage offline. For live mitigation, keeping rollback is safest.
elaine-cs: Notifying affected customers that we've identified a calibration-related regression and have rolled back; update ETA for follow-up postmortem later today.
jess-oncall: Action items so far: rollback confirmed, routing fallback in place, alerts silenced for canary hosts. Monitoring for p95/p99 and stream stall count for next 30 min. @sam-oncall will keep watch for escalation.
sam-oncall: I'll monitor. Quick queries:
```
# p99 over last 15m
sum_over_time(request_latency_p99{route="/v1/stream",region="us-west"}[15m])
# stream stall metric
sum(increase(streaming_stalls_total[5m])) by (host)
```
sam-oncall: currently stalls dropping: {host-int8-04: 18->4, host-fp16-02: 2->1}
jess-oncall: Good. Morgan, can you snapshot the int8 host disk I/O and upload to the incident folder for postmortem? add any core dumps.
morgan-runtime: snapshotting now to s3://redwood-incidents/5067890123-int8-disk-snap.tar.gz. Also saving runtime traces: /incidents/5067890123/traces.tar.gz
alex-sre: Also captured router queue histograms and KV hit/miss ratios. Will attach shortly.
priya-eng: followup plan: run a local repro with long-context streaming + int8-calib kernels to verify the dequant->disk contention. If repro'd, we'll change to async dequant path and add prefetching.
elaine-cs: CS will send templated update to customers at +1h and again after postmortem.
jess-oncall: Escalation? Any customer impact beyond increased latency and occasional truncated streams? @elaine-cs
elaine-cs: No data loss, no PII exposure, some timeouts causing bad UX on a handful of sessions. Customers want an incident timeline and mitigation summary.
deploy-bot: Noted: no further deploys queued to model-path until postmortem signoff.
sam-oncall: p95 trending back to ~150ms, p99 ~240ms now. stalls ~baseline. Looks like rollback brought things under control.
jess-oncall: Great. I'm going to hand off to @sam-oncall for watch and start writing initial incident context in pagerduty ticket. Sam, keep the channel updated and notify if p99 > 500ms again.
sam-oncall: Ack. Taking over watch. I'll update PD and set an automated job to snapshot histograms every 5m for the next 2h.
jess-oncall: Before signing out: please prepare a short blameless postmortem draft capturing timeline, root cause hypothesis (int8 dequant sync path + KV miss spike), mitigations (rollback, routing fallback), and followups (async dequant, prefetch, stricter canary health checks). Assign owners: priya-eng (repro & fix), alex-sre (router KV metrics), morgan-runtime (trace artifacts), elaine-cs (customer comms).
priya-eng: will take ownership of repro & fix. ETA initial PR for async path: 48h.
morgan-runtime: I'll upload all artifacts and a short runtime analysis doc by EOD.
elaine-cs: customer comms drafted, ready to send after final wording check.
sam-oncall: monitoring stable. closing the active paging window now but leaving the channel open for postmortem. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident update: status=mitigated, severity=medium, pages=1, oncall_handoff=completed. Follow-up tag: postmortem-required. Link: <https://redwood.incidents/PD-98765>
